title: S2 v2: execution waves in daemon.dispatch behind [scheduler].mode = shadow|active|off — interference-compatible wave logged to runs/sched/waves.jsonl, applied only in active mode (spec review T-0523 folded in)
spec:
Goal T-0503, brief .orchestrator/adaptive-parallelism-program.md section P3 (select the best set of mutually compatible ready tasks; respect depends_on, capacity, budgets, cooldowns, safety policy) and Evaluation (retain what baseline scheduling would have done). Base goal/T-0503 with S0a (schedlog, dispatch.jsonl considered rows, first_ready_at) and S1 (interference.select_wave, pairwise) merged. Work only in your worktree, commit only on your own branch with the task id in the message, run the full .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh before reporting; report sha and failures only.
Facts: daemon.dispatch walks bus.read(status="queued", role="execute") + retry_held (budget-held tasks with no dispatched_at) in id order and dispatches first-come until free_slots; _load_review_cfg(pool) (daemon.py:217) shows how a pool.toml table is read into module globals with defaults, but it is called only from tick(), and the Daemon tests call daemon.dispatch(pool) directly (tests/test_daemon.py, dispatch_telemetry helper). interference.select_wave(ready, running, tasks, capacity, order=None, graph=None, rules=None) -> {wave, deferred} takes and returns task ids; interference.pairwise(tasks_list) takes task dicts.
1. _load_scheduler_cfg(pool): table [scheduler] with defaults mode = "shadow" (off|shadow|active), soft_conflict_policy = "defer", max_wave = 0 (0 = capacity); called at the top of dispatch(pool) itself (idempotent and cheap) so tests that call dispatch directly observe the mode; tick() needs no extra call. Add the table to .orchestrator/pool.toml with comments (default shadow: dispatch unchanged, waves only logged; active dispatches the wave; off disables both); touch install.py only if pool.toml is templated there.
2. In dispatch, once per tick: candidates = the dispatch-eligible tasks in the existing order: queued execute tasks plus the budget-held retries from retry_held, each ready, non-stale, spec-approved or below SPEC_REVIEW_MIN, with a fallback tier when in fallback mode (budget retries are ordinary candidates; their status held is irrelevant to selection). running = execute tasks with status running plus dispatched-but-unclaimed ones. tasks = a dict id -> task covering candidates, running and their goal siblings. order = _wave_order(candidate_ids, tasks), a module-level hook returning its input unchanged (a later task replaces it). result = interference.select_wave(candidate_ids, running_ids, tasks, capacity=min(slots, max_wave or slots), order=order, rules={"soft_conflict_policy": ...}). predicted = interference.pairwise([tasks[i] for i in result["wave"]]) (ids mapped back to dicts). When mode != off and candidates exist: schedlog.append("waves", {"ts","mode","ready": candidate_ids,"running": running_ids,"baseline_order": the first-come ids that would dispatch within slots,"wave","deferred","predicted","priority": {},"applied": mode == "active"}).
3. mode off or shadow: dispatch exactly as before (first-come). mode active: dispatch the wave in wave order and no other task this tick; each deferred candidate is recorded in the dispatch.jsonl considered row as skipped with reason "predicted_interference" (hard or soft deferral) or "executor_capacity" (capacity deferral). Invariants in every mode: never more dispatches than slots; never a task whose dependencies are not merged; never a hard-conflicting pair co-dispatched in active mode; spec-review creation and the review respawn loop unchanged.
4. README Pipeline section: one paragraph on [scheduler] modes and the waves log.
5. Tests, unittest.TestCase methods in tests/test_daemon.py: test_scheduler_cfg_defaults, test_dispatch_shadow_logs_wave_and_keeps_first_come, test_dispatch_active_defers_hard_conflict_with_running_task, test_dispatch_active_respects_slots_and_dependencies, test_dispatch_mode_off_writes_no_wave_rows, test_dispatch_wave_includes_budget_retry_candidates. Existing tests stay green.
acceptance: tests/test_daemon.py::test_scheduler_cfg_defaults and tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_shadow_logs_wave_and_keeps_first_come pass: [scheduler] mode defaults to shadow, dispatch order and set are unchanged, and every tick with candidates appends a waves.jsonl row with ready, running, baseline_order, wave, deferred, predicted and applied false

tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_active_defers_hard_conflict_with_running_task and tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_active_respects_slots_and_dependencies pass: mode active dispatches only the selected wave, never a hard-conflicting pair together, never beyond free slots or unmet dependencies, and records deferred candidates in dispatch.jsonl as predicted_interference or executor_capacity

tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_mode_off_writes_no_wave_rows and tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_wave_includes_budget_retry_candidates pass: mode off writes no waves rows and dispatches as before; budget-held retries are wave candidates
full .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 and the suite gains six tests

constraints.interface_contract: _wave_order(candidate_ids, tasks) module hook returning an ordered id list (S3 replaces it); _load_scheduler_cfg(pool) called from dispatch; waves.jsonl row {ts, mode, ready, running, baseline_order, wave, deferred, predicted, priority, applied}; [scheduler] keys mode, soft_conflict_policy, max_wave

result.summary: superseded by S2 v3 after spec review T-0525 request_changes (reuse capacity_reason for wave-capacity deferrals; one shared _first_come_order helper for the real path and baseline_order; tasks dict covers transitive depends_on ancestry); no code was written

spec_review_risks.issue: Spec hardcodes reason="executor_capacity" for every wave-capacity deferral in active mode, but dispatch() already computes a capacity_reason local (cooldown | account_capacity | executor_capacity) that existing tests (test_dispatch_logs_cooldown_fallback_budget_and_noop) rely on to distinguish why slots ran out. If interference.select_wave's capacity limit is hit while the real cause is a cooling executor or fallback-account exhaustion (not plain saturation), the new telemetry silently mislabels it as executor_capacity, defeating the per-cause granularity S0a/this ticket's own telemetry goal was built for.

baseline_order ("the first-come ids that would dispatch within slots") requires re-deriving the existing per-task eligibility+slot-decrement logic (verdict, complexity vs SPEC_REVIEW_MIN, fallback-tier availability, slots<=0) as a side-effect-free dry run, since in active mode the real dispatch path no longer performs first-come selection. The spec doesn't name a shared helper for this, so active mode risks a hand-duplicated second copy of the first-come rules living alongside the real one used by off/shadow, which can silently drift out of sync over time.

tasks dict is scoped to "candidates, running and their goal siblings" for interference.classify's dependency-chain walk (_depends_on). If a candidate's depends_on chain passes through a task outside its own goal (cross-goal dependency), _depends_on's walk silently stops at the first id missing from the dict (tasks.get(current, {}) short-circuits to no further depends_on), so a real hard "dependency" conflict could go undetected without any error.
